references.text: Jesus went throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues—a parallel to Luke's description of him teaching in the synagogues.
Matthew again describes that Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, which corresponds to Luke's account of his teaching in the synagogues.
Mark tells us that Jesus entered the synagogue in Capernaum and taught, and people were amazed at his teaching—this corresponds to Jesus being praised by all in Luke 4:15.
Mark describes that Jesus went throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues, a direct parallel to Luke's account of teaching in the synagogues.
The immediately preceding verse tells us that Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread—this forms the context for his being praised by all.
The following paragraph gives a concrete example of Jesus teaching in a synagogue (in Nazareth), where people were first amazed at the gracious words that came from his mouth.
Jesus went down to Capernaum and taught the people on the Sabbaths, and they were filled with wonder at his teaching—yet another example of teaching in the synagogue and a positive response.
Luke summarizes that Jesus continued to preach in the synagogues, confirming the pattern described in verse 15.
Jesus himself says that he has always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all Jews gather—a confirmation of his practice of teaching in the synagogues.
Peter's speech in Acts summarizes how Jesus began in Galilee and was anointed with the Holy Spirit and power—a reference to the same period described in Luke 4:15.
